## SPINE & PM&R EVALUATION NOTE 



PATIENT	DOB	MRN	DATE OF SERVICE
Dax Vance	04/12/2001	940-2281-A	09/12/2022
SUBJECTIVE
Patient presents with persistent mid-cervical pain radiating into the bilateral trapezius. Pain began 6 days ago during a heavy
squat set in the gym. Patient describes pain as a constant deep ache, rated 6/10. Denies upper extremity paresthesias or
weakness.
OBJECTIVE
Cervical spine exam reveals tenderness to palpation from C4 through C6. Significant spasm of bilateral paraspinal muscles.
Range of motion is restricted: flexion 30 degrees (normal 45), extension 15 degrees (normal 45). Bilateral upper extremity
motor and sensory exam is intact.
ASSESSMENT
Acute cervical strain with possible underlying cervical disc herniation or bulge. Rule out disc pathology.
PLAN
Order cervical spine X-ray/MRI. Initiate conservative treatment with physical therapy, stretching, and nonsteroidal anti-
inflammatory drugs. Patient to follow up in 2 weeks.



Dr. Alistair Finch, MD - Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation
